pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule applicable to enterprise registration in Viet Nam

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment or Export Processing/Industrial Zone Management Board
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for foreign-invested project registration, subject to waiver in certain industrial-zone regimes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization, notarization, and sworn Vietnamese translation bundle for approximately four to five foreign corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate abroad, Vietnamese notary office, and certified translation service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular fee schedule plus prevailing notarial and translation market tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening, risk assessment, and evidential file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Vietnamese law firm / AML due-diligence vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for medium-risk enhanced due diligence on one limited liability entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for investment dossier drafting, name-clearance review, Articles of Association preparation, and registration filing support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Pre-agreed fixed legal fee or prevailing hourly-rate market benchmark for Stage 1 work

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical suite reservation and first-month serviced-office deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial serviced-office provider in Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a small corporate-services office package with physical substance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14, especially Articles 24 through 39 and 47 through 78 governing limited liability companies; Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 37 through 38 governing Foreign-Invested Enterprise registration; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP detailing the Law on Enterprises; Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP detailing the Law on Investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office (Phòng Đăng ký kinh doanh) of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI), operating through the National Enterprise Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn); for foreign investors, the Investment Registration Authority under the Department of Planning and Investment for the Investment Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Enterprise Registration Certificate application dossier (Hồ sơ đăng ký doanh nghiệp) culminating in the Enterprise Registration Certificate (Giấy chứng nhận đăng ký doanh nghiệp); a foreign-invested LLC must first or simultaneously obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (Giấy chứng nhận đăng ký đầu tư).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Viet Nam imposes no general statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC, and ISIC 6420 IP holding and patent sub-licensing is not a conditional business line under the Law on Investment 2020 or Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP. The LLC must declare its charter capital in the Company Charter and must pay in 100% of the subscribed charter capital within 90 days after the Enterprise Registration Certificate is issued, as required by Article 47 of the Law on Enterprises. For a foreign-invested entity, the capital contribution schedule is recorded in the Investment Registration Certificate and enforced at company incorporation. Vietnamese law does not require an escrow account; the capital contribution is paid in cash into an ordinary corporate bank account or into the direct investment capital account (DICA) maintained at a commercial bank licensed by the State Bank of Viet Nam.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO FORMA FIRST MEMBERS COUNCIL RESOLUTION OF [__] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (the Company) - Adopted by unanimous written consent of all members on [date] 202_.

WHEREAS the Company is to be incorporated under the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam and the Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP;

WHEREAS the Company will carry on the business of owning and sub-licensing patents, trademarks, and other intellectual property and will be registered as an Intellectual Property HoldCo under ISIC 6420;

NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED:

1. Incorporation: The Chairperson of the Members Council and the General Director (who shall be the legal representative of the Company) are hereby authorized to prepare, execute, notarize where required, and submit the investment registration dossier and the enterprise registration dossier through the National Enterprise Registration Portal, and to receive the Enterprise Registration Certificate on behalf of the Company.

2. Registered Office: The registered office of the Company is fixed at [full address, city/province, Viet Nam]. The General Director is authorized to execute and manage the office lease agreement and to notify the competent authority of any subsequent change of address in accordance with Article 37 of the Law on Enterprises.

3. Share Capital and Contribution: The charter capital of the Company is fixed at VND [value] (and its USD equivalent). The capital is subscribed by the members in the following proportions: [Member A]: [percent]%, [Member B]: [percent]%. Each member shall make its capital contribution in cash to the corporate bank account of the Company no later than 90 days from the date of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate, in accordance with Article 47 of the Law on Enterprises 2020.

4. Officers: The following officer appointments are approved: Chairperson of the Members Council: [name]; General Director and legal representative: [name]; Chief Accountant: [name] or licensed external accounting service provider. The General Director shall enjoy all management powers set out in the Company Charter and the Law on Enterprises 2020.

5. Banking and Payment Rails: The General Director is authorized to open (i) a current operating account, (ii) a direct investment capital account (DICA) where required, and (iii) a royalty collection account denominated in foreign currency with a commercial bank duly licensed by the State Bank of Viet Nam. Cross-border royalty inflows may be received via SWIFT and intercompany wires.

6. Corporate Seal: The Company shall cause a corporate seal to be made under Article 43 of the Law on Enterprises 2020 and shall publish the seal specimen on the National Enterprise Registration Portal.

7. Post-Incorporation Filings: The General Director is authorized to complete tax registration, electronic invoice registration, labor registration if the Company employs personnel, and all other incidental formalities before the tax authority and the Department of Planning and Investment.

This Resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in force until changed by a subsequent resolution of the Members Council.

Approved this [day1] day of [month], 202_.

Chairperson of the Members Council: [signature]
General Director / Legal Representative: [signature]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization, Translation, and Notarization of Incorporation Dossiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Văn phòng Công chứng) accredited by the Ministry of Justice in the province of the registered office; Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Department and Notary Office for consular legalization or apostille of foreign-origin documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each foreign corporate or individual member, obtain the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, and power of attorney; arrange apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention or consular legalization, and obtain a certified notarized Vietnamese translation under the Law on Notarization No. 77/2014/QH13. The translated copies must be certified true copies and executed before the Vietnamese notary. Submit the notarized dossier to the office of the company's legal representative. If an individual legal representative is appointed, retain a notarized copy of his or her passport for later submission.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation or official extract from the corporate register of each foreign corporate member
Apostilled or consular-legalized passport copy of each individual member and legal representative
Resolution of the foreign parent entity authorizing the establishment of the Viet Nam LLC and appointing the legal representative
Power of attorney for submission if the legal representative does not file in person
Certified Vietnamese translation of the company charter of each corporate member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary refuses certification due to formal defects, correct the translation and resubmit to the same or another licensed notary office. If consular legalization or apostille is refused, remedy the missing attestation through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the issuing competent authority of the foreign state; an administrative complaint may be lodged under the Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Acquisition and Verification of the Corporate Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) via the National Enterprise Registration Portal; local building management or land lessor as evidence provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select and execute a lease agreement for a lawful office premises within the territory of the province where the LLC will have its registered office. Verify that the premises is legally owned or lawfully used in accordance with the certificate of land use rights or certificate of ownership, and confirm the lessor's authority to sublease. The lease must clearly describe the exact office address and the permitted use of the premises for administrative and intellectual-property management purposes. Retain notarized Vietnamese copies of the lessor's legal documents for attachment to the enterprise registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Signed office lease agreement for the registered office
Certificate of land use rights, certificate of building ownership, or lawful proof of the lessor's right to lease
Building management confirmation approving use of the premises as a company registered office
Notarized copy of the lessor's identity document or enterprise registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the premises are deemed not lawful for the registered office or the lessor lacks proper title, terminate the lease and substitute another premises; the DPI will accept an amended address declaration through the National Enterprise Registration Portal before issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foreign Investment Project and Issuance of the Investment Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Registration Authority under the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI), filing through the National Single Window Portal (msp.gov.vn)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where the LLC is a foreign-invested enterprise, submit the investment registration dossier electronically or in person to the Investment Registration Authority. The dossier must show the proposed project scale, content (ownership and cross-border sub-licensing of patents and trademarks), registered location, total investment capital, charter capital, and capital contribution schedule. The authority will verify the investor's legal status, financial capacity, infrastructure availability, and the absence of market-access restrictions for ISIC 6420. If the business line is not conditional, the IRC must be issued within 15 working days of receipt of a valid dossier.
required_dossiers: Investment project registration application completed on the statutory form
Certified copies of the legal status documents of the foreign investor (certificate of incorporation or equivalent)
Financial capacity evidence, including audited financial statements or a bank confirmation of available funds
Location dossier and a copy of the office lease agreement
Draft Company Charter and capital contribution schedule
Notarized passport copies of all members and the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI issues a written request for supplementation, the application pause will be stated in that notice; the dossier may be resubmitted without charge through the portal. If the investment registration is refused, the refusal must be reasoned in writing, and the investor may lodge an administrative complaint with the provincial People's Committee or institute administrative proceedings under the Law on Administrative Procedures No. 93/2015/QH13.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Enterprise Registration Application and Issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment via the National Enterprise Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Registration Certificate, file the enterprise registration application for a limited liability company, using the statutory forms promulgated with Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, including the application for enterprise registration, the draft Company Charter, the list of members, and the list of legal representatives. The registered office, governance structure, charter capital, and business lines must be consistent with the IRC. The Business Registration Office will examine the dossier and issue the Enterprise Registration Certificate no later than 3 working days after receipt of a complete and valid dossier. The LLC comes into existence as of the date of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for enterprise registration (Giấy đề nghị đăng ký doanh nghiệp)
Draft Company Charter in the statutory form
List of members and each member's capital contribution (list of authorized representatives if corporate members exist)
List of legal representatives
Certified notarized copies of passports and credentials of the legal representative and members
Certified copy of the Investment Registration Certificate
Copy of the office lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is inadequately completed, the Business Registration Office must issue a written request for supplementation and specify the deficiencies. The enterprise may correct and resubmit the same dossier without prejudice. If the registration is refused, the refusal notice must state the legal grounds, and the applicant may lodge a complaint with the provincial People's Committee or initiate administrative court proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Charter Capital and Opening of Corporate and FDI Capital Bank Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial joint-stock bank or foreign bank branch duly licensed by the State Bank of Viet Nam (SBV)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 90 days of the Enterprise Registration Certificate date, transfer 100% of the subscribed charter capital from the foreign investor's accounts to a corporate bank account in Viet Nam. Open a direct investment capital account (DICA) where required by SBV regulations, and open an ordinary operating account for receipt of royalty payments. The legal representative must complete the bank's anti-money-laundering KYC documentation, provide the corporate seal specimen, the Enterprise Registration Certificate, the Investment Registration Certificate, and the first Members Council Resolution, and sign the account opening mandates. After the capital is paid, obtain a capital contribution certificate or payment evidence and file it in the Company's records and with the DPI if requested.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate
Investment Registration Certificate
First Members Council Resolution approving the accounts and authorized signatories
Corporate seal specimen
Charter capital contribution schedule
Passports and KYC documents of all account authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank refuses to open the account for KYC or policy reasons, select another SBV-licensed bank and accelerate the capital contribution pending the opening of the new account. Any unexplained refusal may be reported to the State Bank of Viet Nam's branch in the province for supervisory review; the 90-day statutory capital deadline remains protected by submitting capital transfer orders once the account is operational.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Electronic Invoice Registration, Seal Publication, and Post-Formation Compliances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Tax Department (Cục Thuế) operating under the General Department of Taxation, accessed via the electronic tax portal; Business Registration Office for seal specimen publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Enterprise Registration Certificate automatically contains the enterprise code and tax code; complete the tax declaration to the Provincial Tax Department by registering the legal representative, signatories, and e-tax accounts. Apply for use of electronic invoices in accordance with Decree No. 123/2020/ND-CP. Make a corporate seal, preserve the seal in accordance with Article 43 of the Law on Enterprises, and publicly post the seal specimen and lawful person information on the National Enterprise Registration Portal within the statutory time limit. If employees are hired, carry out labor registration with the local authority and register the workplace. Submit the certificate of completed capital contribution to the DPI and the tax office if required, and ensure the Company's books are opened from the effective date.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate containing the enterprise code and tax code
Application for electronic invoice registration
Corporate seal specimen notice for the National Enterprise Registration Portal
Capital contribution payment certificates and bank transfer receipts
Labor registration forms and workplace manifests if personnel are employed
List of authorized signatories for tax and electronic invoices
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority does not activate the electronic tax portal after submission, contact the General Department of Taxation and request activation via the hotline; any refusal may be appealed to the provincial People's Committee. If the seal publication fails on the portal, re-submit the seal specimen notice through the National Enterprise Registration Portal and retain the portal confirmation receipt; penalties for late publication are curable by voluntary disclosure to the competent authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure patent and trademark holding and sub-licensing LLC (ISIC 6420). The activity does not appear on Viet Nam's conditional business list under the Law on Investment 2020, Annex IV, and therefore no industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over the core business. If in future the LLC adds manufacturing or another regulated branch, the competent industrial authority would be the Ministry of Industry and Trade or the relevant specialized ministry at the national level, together with the provincial Department of Planning and Investment for an amended Enterprise Registration Certificate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; no separate operational permit is required for cross-border IP patent licensing and royalty collection. The sole statutory instruments are the Enterprise Registration Certificate (Giấy chứng nhận đăng ký doanh nghiệp) and, for a foreign-invested entity, the Investment Registration Certificate (Giấy chứng nhận đăng ký đầu tư), both issued by the provincial Department of Planning and Investment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) and the provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from environmental impact assessment and environmental registration. A non-production, non-manufacturing intellectual-property holding and licensing office is not listed in Annex II or Annex III of Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP and does not fall within the EIA-triggering project categories; the Company is not required to prepare an Environmental Impact Assessment Report or obtain an environmental license.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core licensing activity. The office operation produces only domestic wastewater and municipal solid waste, which must connect to the local municipal wastewater collection network under the Law on Environmental Protection 2020 and, where applicable, comply with Vietnamese national technical regulations for domestic solid waste. No VOC, industrial wastewater, hazardous waste, or stack emission thresholds apply because no industrial process, manufacturing, or physical production is carried out at the registered office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The lessor/building owner of the registered office must hold a valid fire safety design approval and fire safety acceptance certificate under Decree No. 136/2020/ND-CP and the Law on Fire Prevention and Rescue and Prevention of Fire-Related Costs shall be inspected upon practical use by the Fire Prevention and Rescue Police of the provincial Public Security. The Company must carry out occupational risk assessment, maintain first aid equipment, and comply with the Law on Occupational Safety and Health No. 84/2015/QH13; the lessor must provide evidence that the building meets structural load standards (TCVN). Under Viet Nam's civil defense obligations, the Company is required to cooperate with the local People's Committee and the competent police authority on emergency and civil defense notification plans; however, no separate civil defense license is issued to private enterprises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế) under the Ministry of Finance of Viet Nam; national e-tax portal: https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn; national e-invoice portal: https://hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested LLC must first obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) where required and an Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment; upon ERC issuance the tax authority automatically grants a 13-digit Tax Identification Number (Mã số thuế). The company must then complete VAT registration, register for mandatory e-invoicing, and file electronic tax declarations through the national e-tax portal. A foreign contractor without a permanent establishment must procure a tax code by submitting Form 01/DNT-XN (foreign contractor tax registration) on the e-tax portal before executing any royalty or licensing transaction in or with Vietnam.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a resident Vietnamese LLC is taxed as a separate juridical person on worldwide income at the standard 20% CIT rate; no pass-through or partnership flow-through treatment exists. Territorial scope: worldwide income for tax-resident enterprises. Base regime is not a tax-exempt zone; export processing zones, industrial parks, and high-tech parks merely confer CIT and VAT incentive regimes within the same entity-level taxation framework.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam has no check-the-box election and does not recognize hybrid entity classification elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) the Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) deemed taxation method versus the actual computation method under Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC for non-resident licensors and service providers; (ii) election of CIT incentive regimes for qualifying high-tech, supporting-industry, export-processing and large-scale investment projects; (iii) related-party interest limitation and transfer-pricing elections under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, including the 30% EBITDA interest deduction cap; treaty relief is obtained through Vietnamese tax treaty adjustment procedures rather than hybrid mismatch elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT – Thuế Giá Trị Gia Tăng) operating on the destination principle; governed by the Law on VAT No. 48/2024/QH15 (effective 1 July 2025), Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC, and subsequent GDT guidance; special consumption tax and environmental protection tax apply separately to particular goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 100,000,000 in annual taxable turnover; this threshold principally exempts small households and individual business households. LLCs and foreign-invested enterprises are mandatorily required to register for VAT upon issuance of the ERC regardless of projected turnover. Foreign contractors without a local entity must complete FCT registration before supplying licensable transactions or services in Vietnam.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: E-invoicing is mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses since 1 July 2022. E-invoices must contain a digital signature and be transmitted in near real-time to the General Department of Taxation through the national e-invoice portal using GDT-approved APIs or the GDT e-invoice service provider network. Cash-register-generated e-invoices must forward transaction data to the tax authority within one hour. There is no physical fiscal stamp; invoices generated with tax-authority invoice codes constitute real-time fiscal clearance and primary audit evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to exported goods and exported services, including services consumed outside Vietnam, where: (i) an export contract with a foreign customer is duly signed; (ii) goods physically pass customs on a verified export declaration, or services are documented as supplied to a non-resident and consumed entirely outside Vietnamese territory; (iii) payment is received from abroad in freely convertible foreign currency, supported by an inward remittance certificate or foreign-currency bank statement; and (iv) compliant e-invoices and underlying transactional and shipping/licensing dossiers are retained. Patent and trademark sub-licenses granted to foreign licensees may qualify as exported services if the licensed intellectual property is exploited entirely outside Vietnam and the transaction creates no local consumption or nexus. Certified technology transfers may instead qualify for VAT exemption under the Law on Technology Transfer. Licenses used or commercially exploited within Vietnam remain subject to 10% VAT and may trigger Foreign Contractor Tax withholding obligations for the Vietnamese payer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronically cleared export customs record or Customs Outward Manifest)
Commercial Invoice and Export Sales Contract
Bill of Lading or multimodal/international transport document evidencing physical movement of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Vietnamese commercial bank confirming foreign-currency receipt
IP sub-license, trademark, or patent licensing agreement with governing law, royalty, and territorial exploitation provisions
Insurance certificate for CIF/CIP export shipments
Certificate of origin where applicable for tariff or treaty benefit claims
E-invoice transmitted to the national e-invoice portal showing the 0% VAT line
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The General Department of Taxation and the General Department of Customs conduct post-clearance audits, export-verification interviews, and cross-border data matching against customs declarations, e-invoices, and banking records. Fraudulent zero-rating or refund claims are retrospectively clawed back with interest at 0.03% per day on any incorrectly refunded or credited input VAT. Administrative fines range from penalties for incorrect declarations up to three times the evaded tax, together with suspension of export preferences and revocation of export-processing-enterprise status. Serious violations trigger criminal prosecution under the Penal Code, including tax evasion (Article 200), document forgery (Article 341), and smuggling (Article 188), along with blacklisting of the entity and its legal representatives. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day statutory deadline results in reversal of the zero rate, late-payment interest, denial of refunds, and exchange-control sanctions by the State Bank of Vietnam.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Viet Nam (SBV) (Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam), which exercises exclusive foreign-exchange administration powers under the Law on the State Bank of Viet Nam (Law 46/2010/QH12), the Law on Foreign Exchange Administration (Ordinance 28/2005/PL-UBTVQH11 as amended by Ordinance 06/2013/UBTVQH13), Decree 70/2014/ND-CP on the implementation of the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange, and implementing instruments including Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN on foreign-exchange transactions between authorized credit institutions and clients and Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN guiding foreign-exchange management for foreign direct investment activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Viet Nam operates a managed-float regime for the Vietnamese Dong (VND). Current-account convertibility is substantially liberalized for enterprises: cross-border royalty and IP license revenues received by a Vietnamese IP Holding Company are treated as export-of-services proceeds and enjoy unrestricted repatriation into onshore foreign-currency accounts at SBV-licensed banks, provided the underlying license agreements, invoices, tax certificates, and transaction-purpose documents are compliant. Capital-account transactions remain strictly controlled: inbound FDI charter-capital contributions must flow through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at a licensed bank under an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC); foreign shareholder loans require separate SBV registration; and outbound portfolio investments, guarantees, and loans by VN entities require prior approval or registration. Profit and dividend remittance hurdles are manageable but documentary: a foreign-invested enterprise may remit profits and dividends abroad only after filing audited financial statements, completing annual corporate income tax finalization, settling all tax liabilities, and submitting a profit-remittance confirmation through the licensed bank; no separate 'profit extraction tax' applies beyond standard withholding taxes. Practical convertibility frictions include the SBV requirement to evidence economic substance of IP operations, strict use of regulated transaction-purpose codes, the prohibition on onshore banks extending VND credit or deposit facilities to non-residents except under statutory exceptions, monitoring of disguised capital outflows via excessive royalty payments, and the thin offshore VND market; onshore licensed banks are otherwise permitted to convert current-account proceeds to VND at prevailing interbank rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN (amending and supplementing Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN), all export proceeds, including services and royalty income from cross-border IP licensing, must be received into a foreign-currency account at an SBV-licensed credit institution. For exports of goods, the statutory collection window is 90 days from the date of export, unless an extension is approved in writing by the enterprise's licensed bank for justified commercial reasons; proceeds from services and IP/technology licensing may be collected under the contractual payment term agreed between the parties, but the funds must ultimately be credited to an onshore foreign-currency account of the Vietnamese licensing entity and must not be retained offshore beyond the commercial term. There is no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds: enterprises may retain 100% of exported-service/royalty receipts in foreign currency in their accounts, and conversion into VND is required only when the enterprise needs VND for domestic expenditures, such conversion being executed through authorized banks at the prevailing interbank exchange rate. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the applicable statutory or contract-based deadline exposes the enterprise to administrative fines and enhanced regulatory scrutiny under Decree 88/2019/ND-CP as amended by Decree 143/2021/ND-CP. All foreign-currency receipts must be reported by the servicing bank to the SBV under the periodic foreign-exchange statistical regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) in USD/VND; operational current account (VND); foreign-currency transaction account (USD/EUR/JPY) for royalty receipt collection, trade settlement, and dividend remittance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam JSC (BIDV)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA and multi-currency operational settlement account; payroll and treasury concentration account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade (VietinBank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: DICA, operational current account, and trade-finance collateral account for cross-border LC issuance

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (Agribank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account (predominantly VND); DICA not preferred for complex cross-border IP royalty flows

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Technological and Commercial Joint Stock Bank (Techcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account and DICA with digital banking API integration for treasury automation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech digital EMI providers (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Currencycloud, Payoneer) are rated LOW-FEASIBILITY as substitutes for licensed onshore banking in Viet Nam. They are not authorized by the SBV and cannot perform Vietnamese domestic payment settlement in VND, cannot hold a DICA, and cannot issue statutory Vietnamese banking attestations required for IRC/ERC compliance, dividend remittance, or foreign-loan registration. They may serve only a supplementary treasury function: an offshore entity in the group may use an EMI to aggregate small foreign-currency royalty payments from non-Vietnamese sub-licensees, provided (i) the EMI is not used as the payment beneficiary of record under a Vietnamese contract requiring legal invoices, (ii) the funds are periodically repatriated to the licensed onshore bank within the applicable statutory window, and (iii) all contractual documentation, tax filings, and SBV transaction-purpose codes remain executed through the onshore licensed bank. The SBV does not recognize EMI statements as evidence for inward FDI capital registration, and use of an EMI as an intermediary for outbound payments of royalties, taxes, or dividends is prohibited because those outflows require bank verification of underlying agreements, withholding tax certificates, and purpose codes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, licensed Vietnamese banks require the legal representative of a foreign-invested company (or a Vietnamese-resident representative holding a valid, notarized and consular-legalized or apostilled Power of Attorney) to appear in person at the designated branch for the initial corporate account opening interview and signing-card registration. Fully remote or paperless account opening is not recognized under SBV customer-identification regulations and the Law on Anti-Money Laundering 2022 (effective 1 March 2023) implemented by Circular 09/2023/TT-NHNN and Decision 11/2012/QD-NHNN. The physical interview is conducted by the bank's relationship manager and compliance officer, and the bank verifies the identity and authority of signatories against authenticated passport copies and the Enterprise Registration Certificate. For foreign legal representatives located abroad, banks generally permit the physical interview to be performed by an attorney-in-fact whose notarized POA, original passport, and Vietnamese notarized translation are presented, but the foreign UBO must nonetheless pass a remote video-KYC interview where the bank requires identification of the ultimate beneficial owner. Some banks (notably international bank branches in Viet Nam) offer hybrid onboarding with a first physical visit for legal representative and then digital signing for additional authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity - ultimate beneficial owner(s) are non-resident individuals located in high-risk or tax-haven jurisdictions, or the ownership structure embeds trusts, foundations, or shell holding layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and consular-legalized (or apostilled) copies of the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) and Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC); certificate of the list of legal representatives and beneficial owners issued by the business registration authority within the previous 30 days; company charter and notarized minutes of charter-capital contribution; passport copies and KYC questionnaires for every UBO holding 20% or more of the entity; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations supported by audited financial statements and offshore bank reference letters; complete group structure chart; for trusts, the full trust deed, register of settlors, trustees, protectors, and beneficiaries, and FATCA/CRS tax-residence identifiers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP-royalty flows to related parties - high-volume periodic royalty receipts and sub-licensing payments create a characteristic royalty-conduit or transfer-pricing red flag under AML and tax-crime risk typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed, stamped license and sub-license agreements containing economic-substance and substantive-use clauses; certified copies of registered patents and trademarks from the National Office of Intellectual Property of Viet Nam or WIPO designations; complete transfer-pricing documentation file (Form 03/tr and Form 04/tr) demonstrating arm's-length royalty rates under Circular 06/2021/TT-BTC and OECD TP guidelines; independent IP valuation report and comparability analysis; evidence of actual IP policing, technical support, and defense activity; annual royalty calculation schedules and usage reports; proof of corporate income tax and foreign contractor withholding tax remittances on any outbound royalty flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactional purpose ambiguity - SWIFT credits described merely as 'IP fees' without precise contractual nexus, or inflows from third-party accounts where the remitter differs from the contractual licensee, triggering suspicion of layering or sanctions evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or certified copy of the cross-border license agreement with the exact payment schedule; commercial invoice, royalty calculation statement, and VAT invoice (if any); bank's Transaction Purpose Declaration form containing SBV transaction-purpose codes; WHT/CIT remittance certificates issued by the Vietnamese tax authority; proof of IP ownership and licensing chain (statement of account from NOIP); complete KYC file of the contractual counterparty including its corporate registration and UBO declaration; written explanatory note covering any third-party payment, set-off, assignment, or group cash-pooling arrangement, executed under Vietnamese law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Country and sanctions exposure - payments routed through banks in jurisdictions subject to international sanctions or with perceived weak AML frameworks, or counterparties matching entries on OFAC, EU, UN, or Vietnamese restricted-party lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive sanctions-screening reports (OFAC/EU/UN/Vietnam) covering all transacting parties, with zero-hit compliance confirmation and screenshots retained; certificates of tax residency and audited financial statements of each counterparty proving actual business substance; detailed group-chart and governance map with parties-in-interest declarations; commitment to route all payments exclusively through SBV-licensed authorized banks and their clearing correspondents; draft compliance certificates and indemnities in the bank's standard form; for any intermediary involved, the intermediary's KYC file, beneficial-ownership schedule, and SWIFT BIC details.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound FDI capital injection for the VN LLC IP Holding Company must be routed exclusively through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam, in the currency nominated in the Investment Registration Certificate (typically USD or VND). The compliant protocol is: (1) secure the IRC and Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) and open the DICA at the chosen licensed bank using the full KYC package; (2) the offshore parent or shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 remittance from its corporate bank account with a stated purpose code 'Direct Investment Capital Contribution' (Vietnamese: góp vốn đầu tư trực tiếp), referencing the IRC number, DICA account number, and license-entity name; (3) the wire is cleared through the corresponding US dollar lines (e.g., New York CHIPS/Fedwire correspondents) or EUR via the euro clearing system, with both the ordering and beneficiary fields matching the registered parties; (4) upon receipt, the bank verifies the transaction against the IRC registered capital schedule, credits the DICA, and delivers an electronic FDI capital registration confirmation to the SBV's Foreign Investment Monitoring system; (5) the capital is either converted into VND through a spot transaction for working-capital needs or retained as foreign currency depending on forecast treasury requirements; (6) any borrowing from foreign shareholders must itself be registered with the SBV as a foreign loan under Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN and the loan drawdown must also be credited to the DICA (or a dedicated foreign-loan account); (7) subsequent changes to capital contribution timing exceeding the IRC schedule require re-registration with the licensing authority and the bank refuses non-compliant credit if the SWIFT purpose code or remitter name does not match the registered data.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements from the Vietnamese IP licensing HoldCo employ the following clearing rails. Royalty and technology-license payments due by Vietnamese sub-licensees to the HoldCo are received onshore through the foreign-currency or VND operating account; where the HoldCo itself remits royalty shares onward to an offshore head-licensor or sub-licensee network, the disbursement is executed by SWIFT MT103 direct wire after the bank verifies the underlying license agreement, the foreign contractor withholding tax (FCW/FCWT) payment certificates or WHT certificates issued by the Vietnamese tax authority, and the SBV transaction-purpose code covering 'payment of royalty/technology transfer'. For the HoldCo's own procurement of goods and services, standard clearing rails comprise SWIFT MT103/MT202 direct transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) governed by UCP600, issued by the Vietnamese bank upon presentation of the underlying commercial contract, invoice, transport or delivery documents, and license deeds where applicable. All outbound foreign-currency wires require the enterprise to hold sufficient foreign-currency balances in its foreign-currency account, or to purchase currencies from the authorized bank under a spot or forward contract with the completed FX purchase application and purpose declaration. Statutory payment routes (taxes, employees, domestic suppliers) are executed from the VND operating account, while dividends and profit distributions are remitted through the DICA or a dedicated dividend-remittance account using the audited annual financial statements, corporate income tax finalization confirmation, and the profit-remittance certification. The group should maintain an in-house banking structure that does not commingle intercompany funds, as Vietnamese law restricts cross-company cash-pooling without genuine intercompany loan documentation and arm's-length interest reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts (value date T+2) executed with SBV-licensed banks under Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN for immediate conversion of royalty receipts or capital injections
Outright forward FX contracts (tenor between 2 and 365 days) covering documented current-account receivables and payables, including cross-border IP royalty income and dividend remittance plans
FX swap/swap-style contracts (tenor between 2 and 365 days) with authorized credit institutions used as liquidity bridges between foreign-currency receipts and VND expenditures

Cross-currency swaps and interest-rate swaps related to registered foreign loans and permitted under SBV loan regulations; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) and exotic FX options are not permitted onshore for corporate clients and may only be accessed offshore outside the Vietnamese regulatory perimeter without recourse to the local banking license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (CIT) finalization return (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation via the provincial tax office (Cục Thuế) where the FIE LLC is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 90th day after the fiscal year end (31 March for calendar-year LLC); audited financial statements, when required, must accompany or precede the finalization return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative fines up to VND 50,000,000; late-payment interest of 0.03% per day on underpaid CIT; persistent failure may trigger a tax authority forced assessment and enterprise registration strike-off under Law on Enterprises 2020, Article 209

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Personal income tax (PIT) finalization return for the employing LLC (Quyết toán thuế TNCN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial tax office (Cục Thuế) with jurisdiction over the LLC's registered tax address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 90th day after the end of the fiscal year (31 March for calendar-year filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines up to VND 50,000,000; late-payment interest of 0.03% per day; penalties may be applied jointly with CIT finalization in a single tax inspection dossier

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory audited financial statements (Báo cáo tài chính năm đã kiểm toán)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI), the provincial tax office, and the General Statistics Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submission of audited financial statements within 90 days from the fiscal year end (31 March for calendar-year LLC); the independent audit must be completed before that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties for late or non-submission of financial statements and for operating without mandatory audit, typically up to VND 50,000,000; falsified statements may trigger criminal liability under the Penal Code 2015 and strike-off proceedings for recurring non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual FDI investment project implementation report (Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động đầu tư)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Investment Registration Agency / Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) and the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly on or before the 10th day of the first month of the following quarter; annual report due on or before 31 January of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Decree 50/2016/ND-CP and Decree 89/2022/ND-CP, up to VND 50,000,000 for late or inaccurate reports; failure to report investment status may impair project licensing and subsequent tax and registry endorsements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business license fee (Lệ phí môn bài) declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial tax office (Cục Thuế) handling the LLC's revenue and registration records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Paid annually no later than 30 January of the following year; newly incorporated LLCs pay within 30 days of enterprise registration certificate issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.03% per day; administrative fines up to VND 3,000,000 for late payment; chronic non-payment may lead to tax authority enforcement and suspension of business registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual anti-money laundering (AML) compliance and beneficial owner (UBO) information report to the State Bank of Vietnam
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV), Anti-Money Laundering Department; UBO details are co-managed through the national enterprise registration database
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January of the following calendar year for the preceding year; beneficial owner details must be updated in the national enterprise registration database within 10 days of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML administrative fines under Decree 93/2023/ND-CP, up to VND 500,000,000 for serious violations; failure to maintain true UBO records may expose the LLC to enhanced due diligence, frozen transactions, and regulatory restrictions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All foreign-invested enterprises (FIEs) in Vietnam are subject to compulsory independent statutory audit, irrespective of revenue, asset size, or headcount; in addition, the annual tax finalization dossier must be supported by audited financial statements where the company is an FIE, a public-interest entity, or a parent company of a consolidated group (Law on Independent Audit 2011, Decree 17/2012/ND-CP, Law on Enterprises 2020)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS) and the Vietnamese Enterprise Accounting Regime (Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC for enterprises); IFRS is optional in separate financial statements for approved FIEs and certain capital-market entities under the Ministry of Finance IFRS roadmap (Decision 345/QD-BTC of 16 March 2020); consolidated and annual reports must retain the VAS basis unless a specific IFRS application license is obtained

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Viet Nam does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation return; instead, the LLC must (i) disclose ultimate beneficial owners in the enterprise registration dossier and update any change in the national enterprise registration database within 10 days, (ii) include UBO and AML compliance in the annual AML report submitted to the State Bank of Vietnam by 31 January, and (iii) maintain and present UBO records during tax and registry audits; for LLCs with member changes from shareholding transfers, a member register update and shareholder resolution must be filed with the Business Registration Office together with the corresponding tax declaration
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (sổ đăng ký thành viên)
Register of Directors / Members' Council meeting minutes and resolutions
Minute Book and corporate seal register
Beneficial owner identification records and UBO tracing file
Accounting books and original vouchers (kept at registered head office or statutory archive)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,500 per year for a licensed registered-office or corporate-secretarial service provider in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 7,000 per year for a certified audit of an IP-holding LLC by an approved audit firm (Big-4 or reputable local firm)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% standard corporate income tax (CIT) rate under the Law on Corporate Income Tax (Law No. 14/2008/QH12, as amended) and Decree No. 218/2013/ND-CP
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent box or IP-specific preferential rate is available in Vietnam. Standard 20% rate applies to royalty and licensing income. Preferential rates (e.g., 10% for high-technology enterprises or new investment projects in special investment incentive sectors) are not ordinarily applicable to a passive IP HoldCo earning cross-border patent licensing revenue. Small- and medium-sized enterprises may qualify for temporary 15%–17% rates under certain conditions, but an IP HoldCo typically fails the scale test.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly provisional CIT declaration – Form 01/TNDN (Tờ khai thuế TNDN tạm tính quý), filed electronically through the Vietnam National Tax Portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 calendar days following the end of each fiscal quarter (e.g., by 30 April, 30 July, 30 October, and 30 January for a calendar-year taxpayer). If the authorized corporate fiscal year differs, the deadline is 30 days after the end of each fiscal quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise Tax Identification Number of the VN LLC (Mã số thuế)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to the Vietnamese resident LLC; foreign shareholders must supply their own tax identification details when filing separate personal/withholding declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box: Doanh thu phát sinh trong quý
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total quarterly gross revenue, including domestic and foreign-sourced royalty, patent license fees, sub-license fees, and all IP-related consideration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a resident LLC, aggregate all worldwide revenue derived from the IP licensing business; non-resident filing instructions do not apply to this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box: Các khoản chi phí được trừ
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses incurred for the quarter, including legal fees, patent registration and maintenance costs, amortization of acquired patents, external consultants, software, and overhead; each item must be accompanied by legally valid invoices and payment vouchers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident licensees are not filing this form; the VN LLC should deduct only expenses properly economically connected to its worldwide licensing revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box: Tổng thu nhập chịu thuế
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly provisional taxable income after subtracting deductible expenses and applying eligible loss carryforward from prior fiscal years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the resident LLC, taxable income is computed on a worldwide basis under Vietnam CIT; foreign-source income from patent licensing is subject to Vietnamese CIT unless an exemption applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box: Thuế TNDN tạm nộp quý
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional quarterly CIT payable calculated as taxable income multiplied by the applicable CIT rate (usually 20%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The VN LLC must remit this provisional amount. Underpayment by more than 20% relative to the final annual returned amount triggers additional penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late quarterly filing or under-provisional payment is subject to an administrative fine of up to VND 80 million under Decree No. 125/2020/ND-CP plus late payment interest of 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount (Article 59 of Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual CIT finalization return – Form 03/TNDN (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN), together with audited financial statements and the related-party transaction disclosure schedules, filed electronically through the Vietnam National Tax Portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the 90th calendar day after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year VN LLC, the deadline is 31 March of the following year. Additional tax due after finalization must be paid by the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the taxable period (e.g., fiscal year 2025) and the tax administration unit (Cục Thuế / Chi cục Thuế) responsible for the LLC's taxation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reserved for the Vietnamese resident taxpayer entity; non-resident shareholders do not enter data in this field on Form 03/TNDN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Doanh thu bán hàng hóa và cung cấp dịch vụ
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total annual gross revenue from the ownership and sub-licensing of patents and related intellectual property worldwide, including royalties, initial license fees, milestone payments, and sub-license pass-through amounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The VN LLC must report all Vietnamese-source and foreign-source licensing revenue. No treaty exemption is available for domestic CIT at the entity level merely because shareholders are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Các khoản chi phí được trừ
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses of the IP HoldCo, including patent amortization, legal and notarial fees, valuation costs, technical staff salaries, quality-control of licensees, and transfer pricing documentation costs; undocumented, unsupported, or non-economic-substance expenses must be excluded
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC cannot deduct deemed internal royalties paid to itself; sub-license pass-through costs should be documented through actual agreements and third-party or intercompany invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual taxable income after all allowed deductions, loss carryforwards, and exemptions; for an IP HoldCo this normally equals gross royalty income less deductible costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Vietnam taxes residents on worldwide income. Foreign royalty withholding taxes may be creditable unilaterally or under a tax treaty to the limited extent recognized by Vietnamese law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses incurred in prior years that have been carried forward, limited to five consecutive years from the loss year, applied sequentially and not exceeding the current year's taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A VN LLC may use the loss carryforward field only with complete supporting schedules; intercompany restructuring losses are carefully scrutinized and may be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Standard CIT rate of 20%, or alternate preferential rate if validly registered; the LLC must attach its investment registration certificate and CIT incentive approvals
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalty income earned by a passive IP HoldCo is not entitled to the export-processing-enterprise (EPE) 0% rate or manufacturing-based incentives unless real production exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Thuế TNDN phải nộp trong năm/nộp bổ sung
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final annual CIT payable after offsetting quarterly provisional payments; any deficit must be paid by the 90th-day deadline, and any overpayment can be offset or refunded
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a resident LLC, the final annual CIT is the full corporate tax liability; no dividend withholding tax is imposed at the enterprise level on distributions to shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Phụ lục giao dịch liên kết (Form 01, 02, 03 under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosures of all related-party transactions, including intercompany patent licensing, royalty rates, sub-licensing agreements, financial capacity, DEMPE functions, and transfer pricing adjustments applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IP HoldCo must explain the economic substance, functions, assets, and risks of each related-party IP arrangement; failure to demonstrate substance may lead to recharacterization of the royalty transaction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual finalization return attracts administrative fines escalating to VND 100 million depending on the number of days overdue. Where underdeclaration exceeds 20% of the final tax, penalties range from 20%–100% of the underpaid tax under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; late payment interest accrues at 0.03% per day. Directors may be subject to personal liability for repeated non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% at the corporate shareholder level. Vietnam does not impose dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a Vietnamese resident company (VN LLC) to foreign corporate shareholders. Non-resident individual shareholders are subject to personal income tax at 5% on dividend income. Repatriation of after-tax profit to foreign corporate owners is generally unrestricted and subject only to exchange control documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because no dividend withholding tax exists in Vietnam, treaty relief is most relevant for outbound royalty and interest payments. To claim a reduced rate under a Vietnam tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of its residence jurisdiction; (2) provide the Vietnamese payer a written beneficial ownership declaration confirming that the recipient is the true economic beneficiary, has no permanent establishment in Vietnam, and is not a conduit; (3) submit the TRC and treaty relief file to the Vietnamese payer before remittance so that the payer can claim treaty application when withholding and remitting tax; (4) retain the entire file for a 10-year audit period. The Vietnamese tax authority may deny or claw back relief if the recipient lacks economic substance or if the transaction is considered abusive under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Vietnamese payer to a non-resident are subject to Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) under Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC: CIT assessed at 10% on gross royalty income and VAT at 5%, unless a treaty reduces the CIT component. Where the recipient is a resident of a Vietnam tax treaty country, the treaty CIT rate on royalties is typically 10% (varies by treaty, with some treaties setting 7.5%, 15%, or 20% for copyright royalties; patent royalties are generally covered by Article 12). Interest paid to a non-resident is subject to FCT CIT at 5% of gross interest; VAT is generally not imposed on interest. Treaty interest rates commonly range from 10% to 15%, but domestic FCT of 5% is often the applicable ceiling for banking institutions. The payer has a statutory obligation to withhold these FCT amounts and, without proper treaty relief, the VN LLC as the remitter will be jointly liable for un-withheld tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Decree No. 132/2020/ND-CP, a Vietnamese enterprise must prepare and maintain a Local File and Master File when it has related-party transactions and (a) annual total revenue exceeds VND 50 billion, or (b) the total value of related-party transactions exceeds VND 30 billion for the fiscal year. In addition, a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory if the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue exceeds VND 18,000 billion (approx. USD 800 million). The VN LLC, as an IP HoldCo with cross-border licensing to affiliates, will almost certainly satisfy one or both thresholds and accordingly must prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation with audited benchmarking analysis.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) — preferred for patent royalty rates where comparable arms-length licenses exist
Resale Price Method — appropriate for distribution/sub-license arrangements
Cost Plus Method — for intercompany R&D and IP-related technical services
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) — the most common fallback for IP sub-license and royalty pooling
Profit Split Method — used when both parties contribute unique intangible value and integrated IP exploitation occurs
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam has not enacted standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) similar to the UAE or Cayman Islands. However, the Vietnamese tax administration applies the substance-over-form doctrine, a statutory General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14, and the beneficial-ownership clauses in tax treaties. For an IP HoldCo, economic substance is evaluated through the DEMPE framework (Development, Enhancement, Maintenance, Protection, and Exploitation). The VN LLC must employ qualified local personnel, maintain board minutes and decision-making records, incur substantive operating expenditures in Vietnam, control the risk profile of the patents, and actually generate revenue from licensing. If tax authorities conclude that the Vietnamese entity is a shell or lacks the capacity to own and exploit the IP, they may recharacterize the royalty income, disallow deductible licensing costs, increase CIT liability, deny treaty benefits on outbound payments, and impose penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting or understating worldwide royalty receipts on Form 03/TNDN; issuing or using false invoices to inflate deductible expenses; maintaining undisclosed offshore accounts; backdating license agreements; or submitting forged tax residence certificates to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine equal to 1–3 times the evaded tax amount under Article 17 of Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; for criminal tax evasion, a fine of up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment of up to 7 years under Article 200 of the Penal Code (No. 100/2015/QH13, as amended). Offending assets may be seized, and the CTA or customs authorities can issue protective seizure orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, and chief accountants may be personally liable for signing false returns. The corporate veil can be pierced where the LLC is operated as an alter ego or fraud instrument; the individual faces civil restitution, travel ban and exit-immigration suspension, loss of limited liability for the unpaid tax, and potential imprisonment as joint offender.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misdeclaration and Shell IP Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany patent royalty rates outside arm's length; paying substantial royalties from Vietnam to an overseas related company that lacks real R&D, ownership, substance, or DEMPE functions; failing to produce the mandated Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country report; using intercompany royalty to strip Vietnamese taxable profit and avoid CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may adjust revenue, disallow excessive royalties, impose the difference in CIT, apply late payment interest at 0.03% per day, and levy administrative penalties of up to 20% of the underpaid tax for incorrect transfer pricing declarations. Failure to submit documentation can trigger fixed fines up to VND 80 million and evidentiary burden reversal, allowing the tax office to apply its own estimates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or knowingly implement sham TP arrangements can be held personally liable to the tax authority. Thailand? The Vietnamese court or tax administration may pierce the corporate veil if the IP HoldCo is a mere shell; officers may receive travel bans and be barred from leaving Vietnam pending tax debt settlement, and criminal charges for intentional violation of tax law can result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Profit Repatriation and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising dividends or equity returns as patent royalties; routing payments through a conduit jurisdiction with a favorable tax treaty while the recipient has no substantive business operations; executing a circular licensing structure where no real IP value flows; or repatriating profits without maintaining the legal and documentary formalities required by the Investment Law and Circular 103/2014/TT-BTC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Vietnam tax authority will deny treaty relief, impose the full FCT rates (10% CIT + 5% VAT on royalties), reclassify the excessive royalty as a dividend or capital contribution refund, and assess penalties plus late payment interest of 0.03% per day. For serious cross-border profit stripping, criminal prosecution for tax evasion may apply, together with asset seizures and sanctions on offshore bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and controlling shareholders who orchestrate phantom royalty structures may have the corporate veil pierced in restitution proceedings; they are personally responsible for unpaid corporate taxes and interest. Personal travel restrictions and entry bans may be issued by the tax authority; if the transaction is found to be in bad faith, civil fraud damages and imprisonment of up to 7 years can be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing via License Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using intercompany or third-party license payments to transfer criminal proceeds through Vietnam; structuring royalty payments to avoid the foreign contractor tax reporting thresholds; accepting payments from high-risk jurisdictions without performing beneficial owner due diligence; or failing to maintain accurate books and records for patent sale or license transactions as required by the Anti-Money Laundering Law (No. 11/2022/QH15).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the AML law and its implementing decrees, license suspension or revocation of the certificate of investment, and criminal liability under Articles 324 of the Penal Code for money laundering, with punishments up to 15 years' imprisonment and fines up to VND 5 billion. The State Bank of Vietnam and tax inspection teams can freeze accounts and halt remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally sanctioned for failure to report suspicious transactions. The corporate veil is disregarded where the LLC is used as a conduit for money laundering; individuals face confiscation of assets, civil restitution to the State, travel bans for suspect persons, and extended terms of imprisonment for systemic AML violations within the enterprise.
